cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Hope Keeps Moving
cards.instruction: Turn every disappointment into a new reason the desired outcome is delayed, redirected, or becoming more meaningful.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll find our wedding venue. The hall said no; we're meant to have somewhere less municipal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Every venue is booked for June.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you choose a September weekend. Three more months to practise being married.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My parents can't travel in September.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll go to them. Ask about their garden; I'll do the arranging. We're finding where this wedding belongs.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 takes venue leadership and interprets rejection as a better direction; A3 yields weekend selection; A5 offers arranging while B asks parents, treating the new location as meaningful.

responseLogic.evidence: June to September provides three more months; B4 travel limit is met by a proposed visit, with A5 explicitly asking about garden availability.

relationship.evidence: B2 supplies actual availability constraints and B4 wants parents included.

heightening.evidence: B4 parents inability to travel causes A5 to move the proposed wedding and reinterpret its proper place.

specificity.evidence: A1 wedding venue and B2 June establish the plan; B4 family constraint explains the final redirection.
